questions.question: Which of following silver coins was introduced by Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish?
questions.solution:
• Iltutmish's Silver Coin: Tanka
  • Fact: He also introduced the copper coin known as the Jittal. These two coins formed the basis of the Sultanate's currency system.

questions.question: When was the Lahore declaration signed between India and Pakistan?
questions.solution:
• Lahore Declaration: February 1999
  • Context: Signed by PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Nawaz Sharif to promote peace and stability between the two nuclear-armed nations.

questions.question: The part of a temple wherein the main deity of the temple is housed is known as the _______.
questions.solution:
• Main Deity House: Garbha Griha
  • Architecture: Literally meaning 'womb chamber', it is the small, dark sanctum sanctorum where the idol (Murti) is placed.

questions.question: The Early Vedic economy was primarily based on_________ activity.
questions.solution:
• Early Vedic Economy: pastoral
  • Detail: Wealth was measured in cows (Gau), and the Rig Veda describes society as semi-nomadic cattle-rearers.

questions.question: In which of the following cities was the first successful textile mill established in India in the year 1854?
questions.solution:
• First Textile Mill: Bombay
  • 1854: Founded by Cowasji Nanabhoy Davar, marking the beginning of the modern Indian cotton industry.

questions.question: After the ________ of Hakim Mirza, Kabul was annexed by Akbar and given to Raja Man Singh as ‘jagir’.
questions.solution:
• Kabul Annexation: death
  • History: After the death of his half-brother Mirza Hakim in 1585, Akbar integrated Kabul directly into the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Harshvardhan's ambitions of extending his power to Deccan and South India were stopped by:
questions.solution:
• Harshvardhan's Defeat: Pulakesin II
  • Battle: Fought on the banks of the Narmada River. Pulakesin II was the greatest ruler of the Chalukyas of Vatapi.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct in context of Buddhist architecture?

i. Uddeshika stupa was created as a memorial.

ii. Paribhogika stupa contained the buried bodily remains of Buddh

iii. Bharhut stupa is situated in Uttar Pradesh.
questions.solution:
• Buddhist Stupa Facts: Only i and ii
  • Correction: Bharhut stupa is actually located in Madhya Pradesh, not Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: The famous Qila-i-Kuhna (mosque of the old fort) was built by:
questions.solution:
• Qila-i-Kuhna: Sher Shah
  • Location: This mosque is located inside the Purana Qila in Delhi and represents a transition from Lodi to Mughal architecture.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first subcontinental empire?
questions.solution:
• First Subcontinental Empire: Mauryan Empire
  • Note: Under Ashoka, it covered almost the entire subcontinent except for the extreme southern tip.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Law and Justice Minister of independent India?
questions.solution:
• First Law Minister: BR Ambedkar
  • Legacy: Known as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution, he served in Nehru's first cabinet.

questions.question: Who was the first feudatory of Pallavas?
questions.solution:
• First Pallava Feudatory: Vijayalaya
  • Shift: He was a feudatory of the Pallavas who later captured Thanjavur and founded the Imperial Chola dynasty.

questions.question: What kind of structures are generally used by Buddhists for containing remains of their monks and nuns?
questions.solution:
• Relic Containers: Stupas
  • Symbolism: Stupas represent the enlightened mind of the Buddha and serve as burial mounds for sacred relics.

questions.question: The Hathigumpha Inscription was inscribed in which of the following historical regions of India?
questions.solution:
• Hathigumpha Inscription: Kalinga
  • Ruler: It records the military and religious achievements of King Kharavela in the Udayagiri caves near Bhubaneswar.

questions.question: Which of the following events took place in the year 1928?
questions.solution:
• Event of 1928: Bardoli Satyagraha
  • Leader: Led by Vallabhbhai Patel; its success earned him the title 'Sardar'.

questions.question: The excavated ruins of the Nalanda University indicate that bright red _____ was/were used in its construction.
questions.solution:
• Nalanda Construction: bricks
  • Archaeology: The world's first residential university was built primarily using high-quality burnt red bricks.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Child Marriage Restraint Act passed?
questions.solution:
• Child Marriage Act: 1929
  • Sarda Act: Named after Harbilas Sarda, it fixed the minimum age of marriage for girls at 14 and boys at 18.

questions.question: In which of the places was Arya Samaj founded?
questions.solution:
• Arya Samaj Birthplace: Bombay
  • 1875: While it became very popular in Lahore later, it was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in Bombay.

questions.question: The rock-cut temple of Shiva built by Krishna I is found at which of the following places?
questions.solution:
• Kailash Temple: Ellora
  • Marvel: This massive rock-cut Shiva temple (Cave 16) was carved out of a single monolithic rock.

questions.question: In India, who introduced the idea of the poverty line for the first time?
questions.solution:
• Poverty Line Idea: Dadabhai Naoroji
  • Method: In his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', he calculated the cost of a 'subsistence diet' for the first time.

questions.question: Tirot Sing was the leader of which of the following revolts?
questions.solution:
• Tirot Sing: Khasi uprising
  • Revolt: He was a Khasi chief who led a resistance against the British attempt to build a road through the Khasi Hills in Meghalaya.

questions.question: The Dravidian style of temple architecture can be largely seen from which part of India?
questions.solution:
• Dravidian Style: Southern India
  • Region: Found between the Krishna River and Kanyakumari, characterized by pyramid-shaped 'Vimanas'.

questions.question: Which chronicler of the medieval age recognised that Raziyya was more able and qualified than all her brothers?
questions.solution:
• Chronicler Minhaj-i-Siraj: Minhaj-i-Siraj
  • Fact: In his work 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri', he honestly admits Raziyya's superiority over her brothers, despite the era's prejudices.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Alexander invade Punjab and in which of the following years did he die?
questions.solution:
• Alexander's Timeline: 326 BC and 323 BC
  • History: He fought Porus at the Battle of the Hydaspes in 326 BC and died in Babylon in 323 BC.

questions.question: Who excavated the Chira Tope stupa at Taxila?
questions.solution:
• Chira Tope Stupa: John Marshall
  • Discovery: Sir John Marshall conducted the major excavations at Taxila (now in Pakistan).
